acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — movers can pack for you, at three levels: full packing (the whole home), partial packing (the rooms or items you choose), and fragile-only packing (just the breakables). Whichever level you choose is scoped room by room and quoted inside the one flat rate in writing before move day — never hourly. Packing can also be booked on its own, without a move attached: packing only is one of the move types on our quote form.

A trained crew packs nearly every item in the home: kitchen, closets, decor, garage. Furniture is protected separately — our published wrap standard is furniture fully covered in padded moving blankets and sealed with clear stretch wrap. Full packing is chosen most for large households, hard closing deadlines, and long-distance moves, where boxes ride for days and must be packed to travel, not just to carry.

The middle level: you pack what you are comfortable packing — clothing, books, linens — and the crew packs the rooms or item classes you assign. The most common assignment is the kitchen, because it is the slowest room in the house to pack well. Partial packing is also the rescue level — if you started packing yourself and ran out of time, a crew can be scoped to finish exactly where you stopped.

Fragile-only packing covers the items where skill matters most: dishes and glassware, artwork and mirrors, TVs, lamps, china and crystal, antiques. They are packed with care and marked FRAGILE. Fragile and high-value pieces escalate past the box when a box is not enough: a large mirror, a marble top, or an irreplaceable antique goes to white-glove handling or a custom-built crate. Name these pieces when the job is scoped — not on move day.

mainEntity.name: Is packing included in a moving quote, or is it an add-on?

acceptedAnswer.text: With most movers, packing is an add-on you must ask for, and many companies bill it by the hour. Our model is different and published: the packing level is scoped with the rest of the job — the items, the distance, the manpower, the equipment — and quoted inside the one flat rate in writing before move day. There is no hourly packing clock.

Even on a full pack, some things a crew cannot take: hazardous materials — paint, solvents, propane, fuel — and perishables are the standard exclusions, and federal guidance is blunt that hazardous materials must never be hidden in household goods boxes. Plants travel badly and are usually excluded too. Irreplaceables — jewelry, documents, medication, cash — should travel with you, whoever packs the box.

mainEntity.name: Does it matter who packs the box?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Under the federal rules for interstate moves, a mover's liability can be reduced by your own acts — the FMCSA consumer booklet gives the example of improper packing of containers you pack yourself. If a box you packed arrives with the carton intact but the contents broken, fault is much harder to establish. The reading is simple: the more breakable and valuable the item, the stronger the case for having the crew pack it.

We do not publish a packing price list, because honest packing cost depends on what is actually being packed — rooms, fragile pieces, crates. Full, partial and fragile-only packing are scoped to your rooms and items, then fixed inside the one flat rate in writing. What changes the scope: number of rooms, fragile and high-value pieces, custom crates, ISPM 15 export packing, and unpacking at destination.

Unpacking and placement at destination: boxes unpacked and items placed, so rooms come back together in order. Unpacking is part of the same service — boxes opened at the destination and contents set out, so the new home is usable the day you arrive.
